extracted.intended_audience: Peer reviewers for Elsevier journals using Editorial Manager's new peer review experience
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and practical standards for peer reviewers using Elsevier's Editorial Manager (new peer review experience) to access manuscripts, write comments, submit recommendations, and manage reviewer confidentiality and metadata (e.g., ORCID).

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to invitation
rubrics_metrics.description: You will receive an email from the journal, inviting you to review the manuscript. The email includes the paper's title, abstract, and the peer review deadline. You can choose whether to accept or decline the invitation via the links in the email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both links in the email direct you to EM; the submission is available in your ‘New Reviewer Invitations’ folder. If you agree to review, the submission appears in your ‘Pending Assignments’ folder. If you decline to review, you can add the reason to decline and suggest alternative reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessing the manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: To start your review, go to your ‘Pending Assignments’ folder in EM and access the manuscript you agreed to review. Click the ‘View and review manuscript’ action link.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The link takes you directly to the new peer review experience, where you can read the manuscript and add your comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the integrated review interface for context
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial Manager’s new peer review experience contains all reviewer comments, author responses to these as well as editor comments together in one single place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this consolidated view to see prior reviewer comments, author rebuttals/responses, and editor notes to inform your assessment and make timely, efficient communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow journal-specific reviewer guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Before writing your reviewer comments, make sure you familiarize yourself with any journal-specific guidelines (these are noted in the journal’s guide for authors available on each journal's homepage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On Elsevier's site, the 'How to conduct a review' page offers useful guidance and suggested questions to take into account while reviewing. Check journal homepage guidance before preparing comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain reviewer anonymity (no identifying information)
rubrics_metrics.description: IMPORTANT: When providing comments, do not include any personal information, such as your name, email address, or any identifying details in the text of your review. Your feedback must remain anonymous to the author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not reveal affiliations, acknowledgements, or other metadata in comments meant for authors. Use editorial-manager features (e.g., 'Notes to editor only') for content that might identify you and that should remain confidential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Download manuscript for reading
rubrics_metrics.description: Click the ‘Download manuscript’ button on the right side of the review page to view the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may download files to read offline or save for detailed inspection; use the Download button rather than copying from the interface.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add comments for the author (public to author)
rubrics_metrics.description: To add comments to the author, navigate to the ‘Comments for author’ tab within the review interface. Click on this tab to open the comment box, where you can type your comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once you enter your comments and click ‘Post’ to submit them, the author can see your feedback. Use this field for substantive, anonymized feedback intended for authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Edit a posted comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Locate your previous comment in the ‘Comments for author’ tab. Click on the three dots icon on the right-hand side of your comment, then select Edit comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the necessary changes in the text box that appears and click ‘Save’ to update your comment. Use edits to correct errors, clarify points, or remove unintended identifying information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add confidential comments to the editor
rubrics_metrics.description: To add feedback that is only visible to the editor, click on the ‘Notes to editor only’ tab. Enter your comments in this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These comments are confidential and are not visible to the author. Use this channel to raise sensitive concerns (e.g., ethical issues, suspected plagiarism, identity disclosure) or to give candid recommendations that should not be shown to authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide overall recommendation and manuscript rating
rubrics_metrics.description: Navigate to the ‘Recommendations’. From the dropdown menu, select your overall recommendation for the manuscript. Additionally, you have the option to provide a manuscript rating to further specify your review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After selecting recommendation and optional rating, ensure you save them by clicking on ‘Save’. Ratings and the recommendation term are recorded separately from comments (note visibility rules below).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit your completed review to the editor
rubrics_metrics.description: After you add your comments and select your recommendation, click on ‘Send review to editor’ to submit your review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once the review is successfully submitted, a confirmation message appears indicating that your review is sent to the editor. Submission finalizes your report; follow journal deadlines and revision policies when submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add completed review to ORCID (opt-in)
rubrics_metrics.description: On the confirmation page after submission, you will see an ORCID section with the option 'Add review to your record.' Click 'Add review' to proceed. You will be asked to provide consent to update your ORCID record with your review activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select 'Yes' to authorize Editorial Manager to deposit the reviewer credit to your ORCID record. If not signed in to ORCID, a one-time ORCID authorization may be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know what review details are visible to authors
rubrics_metrics.description: All reviewer comments are visible to the authors. Authors cannot see reviewer names or personal details, confidential comments to the editor, star ratings, or the recommendation term the reviewer has provided to the editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When drafting public comments, assume authors will see them verbatim (except identifying metadata). Use 'Notes to editor only' for anything authors should not see; star ratings and recommendation terms remain internal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing revised submissions - consult previous materials
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewing a revised manuscript, you can see the comments you provided in the original submission, as well as comments from other reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Click ‘View and review manuscript’ to access the revised paper, review the author’s responses and revisions, refer to your earlier comments, and add your new feedback based on the updated version. When complete, select your recommendation and click ‘Send review to editor’ to submit the updated feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare offline but post and submit online
rubrics_metrics.description: You can download the manuscript file and prepare your review report offline if you prefer. However, you must return to the new peer review experience in your browser to post your comments, provide your recommendation, and submit your completed review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drafting offline is allowed (e.g., in a Word document), but final posting and submission must occur in Editorial Manager to ensure proper recording and anonymity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Device compatibility — desktop/laptop required
rubrics_metrics.description: New peer review experience is not available on mobile, please use other devices to view the links.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access and submit reviews only via a web browser on a desktop or laptop. Mobile devices are not supported for viewing or submitting reviews in the new peer review experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safari popup blocker workaround for Mac users
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a known issue with Safari users due to popup blockers in EM. In the meantime, new peer review experience users on Mac with the latest version of Safari can follow these steps as a workaround: Right-click on the tab URL. Select 'Settings for editorialmanager.com'. In the new popup, locate the 'Pop-up Windows' row. Click on the current value (e.g., 'Block' or 'Block and Notify') and select 'Allow' from the dropdown menu.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a temporary workaround until the EM product team fixes the issue. Use these steps so links and popups necessary for the review workflow function properly in Safari.
